document.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Reagan-Gorbachev, Second Plenary Meeting, Geneva, November 19, 1985
document.authors: U.S. record of Reagan-Gorbachev summit (Ronald Reagan Presidential Library)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Soviet Withdrawal from Afghanistan 1989 | National Security Archive
document.note: Serious US-Soviet dialogue on Afghanistan started in 1985. At Geneva Gorbachev said the Soviets were ready for a package solution: non-aligned Afghanistan, Soviet troop withdrawal, refugee return and international guarantees. Reagan supported 'mutual withdrawal of all outside forces', working through the UN, and a 'coalition of Islamic states' to supervise elections. A month earlier the Politburo had decided in principle to withdraw.

events.description: Second plenary meeting between Reagan and Gorbachev at Maison Fleur d'Eau, Geneva, 2:30-3:40 PM, discussing regional conflicts including Afghanistan, SDI and arms control.
Gorbachev offers a package solution on Afghanistan: non-aligned status, Soviet troop withdrawal, refugee return, international guarantees against interference.
Reagan proposes mutual withdrawal of all outside forces from Afghanistan and a coalition of Islamic states to supervise a government chosen by the Afghan people.
Second Plenary Meeting between Reagan and Gorbachev delegations at Maison Fleur d'Eau, 2:30-3:40 PM.
Private Reagan-Gorbachev meeting held earlier that morning.
Gorbachev rejects U.S. view of Soviet expansionism in Afghanistan, Angola and South Yemen, and denies the Soviets caused revolutions in Afghanistan and Ethiopia.
Gorbachev proposes a package Afghan solution: non-aligned Afghanistan, Soviet troop withdrawal, return of refugees, international guarantees against interference.
Gorbachev argues on strategic parity and opposes SDI as leading to an arms race in space.
Second plenary meeting of Reagan and Gorbachev at Geneva covering SDI, arms reductions, and regional issues; ended at 3:40 p.m. with a private walk.
Gorbachev asserted that SDI would spark an offensive arms race in space and threatened a Soviet buildup in response.
Reagan proposed mutual withdrawal of outside forces from Afghanistan and a coalition of Islamic states to supervise a government.
US offered to place all nuclear weapons under international control.
Reagan proposed guidelines to negotiators for 50% reduction of nuclear weapons.
Reagan and Gorbachev departed for a private walk at 3:40 p.m.

key_claims: Gorbachev denied Soviet expansionist aims in Afghanistan and said Moscow would support a UN-brokered political settlement.
Gorbachev offered a package solution: non-aligned Afghanistan, Soviet troop withdrawal, refugee return, and international guarantees of non-interference.
Gorbachev accused the US of not helping and of effectively wanting Soviet troops to stay in Afghanistan.
Reagan said Afghanistan's leader was supplied by the Soviet Union and that the invasion created three million refugees.
Reagan proposed mutual withdrawal of all outside forces and an Islamic-state coalition to supervise a government chosen by the Afghan people.
